description:
A cursor is a parameter's shape only if something takes it apart. Byte alignment is a cursor fact. A whole-subject guard reads lanes, not a rebuilt rest.

Today:
- An accumulator loop `loop(n, acc <> "ab")` carries acc as a cursor (binary + bit position; transport.rs:169-174, world.rs:560) just because a later byte_size takes a binary_cursor. Every <> then rebuilds the binary from (source, 0): +169 instructions per iteration, 279 vs 448 (M7b/c).
- The non-tail byte loop re-tests pos & 7 every byte and carries an unaligned ldrh/rev16 arm, although the cursor starts at 0 and advances by 8. It also repeats the kind dispatch twice per byte (M10, C9).
- A `byte_size(s) == 0` first clause makes the rest whole via make_cursor_whole (dispatch_subject_var, receive.rs:1497). JSON proposal P3 measured 65 bitstrings and 135 views per 200-byte walk.
- make_cursor_whole makes an FFI call even at a known position 0 (C7).

Fix:
- Cursor shape is demanded only by uses that take the value apart.
- A value produced by <> or a constructor is at position 0 by construction.
- Alignment is a lane fact, set after byte-multiple fields.
- Kind dispatch of a loop-invariant lane is hoisted in the non-tail case, as the tail case already does.
- Guards on byte_size read the lanes.

Folds the receive half of fz-sc8.231. Its handler half needs a runtime ABI change and stays there; split it. Also folds JSON P3.

Asm first: targets for p01b (non-tail match), p03c and a guard-first walk.

Acceptance: slopes as predicted (on bench), and JSON P3's allocation counts fall.
title: A cursor is a shape only where it is taken apart; alignment is a lane fact
